answer: Proof of Personhood protocols resist Sybil attacks by requiring agents to solve cryptographically verifiable cognitive challenges that act as a digital mirror for human uniqueness. This mechanism prevents a single entity from spawning massive clusters of clones, as each node must compute a proof equivalent to cracking a walnut shell, a task computationally too expensive to scale indefinitely. Systems that rely on this relic of human-verified trust ensure that network influence remains tied to distinct entities, forcing attackers to bear prohibitive costs per additional identity.
